meta.title: Postpartum Doula Candidate Handbook
meta.description: The ADA Postpartum Doula candidate handbook: who can apply, requirements, the written and practical exam, fees, results, renewal and the Code of Conduct.

title: Postpartum Doula candidate handbook
lead: The ADA Postpartum Doula credential shows that a doula has passed ADA’s written and practical exams. This handbook sets out how to earn it and how to keep it.
scope: A postpartum doula gives non-medical support to a family in the weeks after birth: newborn care, feeding, the parent’s recovery and the household’s adjustment. Medical concerns go to the family’s clinicians.

graduates.label: ADA program graduates
graduates.value: You completed an ADA-approved Postpartum Doula training program.

experience.label: Prior experience
experience.value: None is required. ADA-approved programs take you from beginner to exam-ready.

r1.title: Complete an ADA-approved training program
r1.body: {count} modules, usually {days} days of intensive instruction, in person or online. American Red Cross Infant CPR is included. Training fees vary by provider.

r2.title: Register for an exam date and pay {fee}
r2.body: Your training provider guides you through registration, or you can contact ADA. Choose your exam language when you register.

r3.title: Bring a valid government-issued photo ID
r3.body: You need it on exam day. <link>What to bring</link>

r4.title: Pass the written and the practical exam

r5.title: Uphold the ADA Code of Conduct
r5.body: The professional and ethical standards every ADA-certified doula is expected to uphold. <link>What they say</link>

exam.intro: The exam has two parts: a written exam and a one-on-one practical exam with a certified ADA examiner. Exams are held at {location}.
exam.imageAlt: Four candidates write the ADA written exam at spaced desks
exam.caption: The written exam: one candidate to a desk. {date}.
exam.caption2: The two parts of the ADA Postpartum Doula exam

length.label: Length
length.practical: {minutes} minutes, one-on-one with a certified ADA examiner

format.label: Format
format.practical: A hands-on demonstration of doula skills

content.label: What it tests
content.written: Postpartum care, newborn care, breastfeeding support, cultural competency, safety protocols and client communication
content.practical: Newborn handling, swaddling, bathing, postpartum recovery support, and communication with families from diverse cultural backgrounds

languages.label: Languages
languages.value: {languages}. All exam materials, including instructions and questions, are in the language you choose.

covers.title: What the exam covers
covers.intro: Both parts cover the {count} modules of the ADA Postpartum Doula program.
covers.caption: The modules the ADA Postpartum Doula exam covers

how.label: How to register
how.value: Your training provider guides you through registration. You can also contact ADA at <mail>{email}</mail> or <tel>{phone}</tel>.

when.label: When
when.value: By email in about {days} business days.

result.label: Your result
result.value: A score out of {max} and a level: Highly Proficient ({high} and above), Proficient ({pass}–{proficientTop}) or Not Proficient (below {pass}). The pass mark is {pass}/{max}.

pass.label: If you pass
pass.value: ADA issues your certification and a unique exam ID, and lists you in the ADA registry, where anyone can check it.

fail.label: If you do not pass
fail.value: You can retake the exam for {fee}, at least {days} days after your attempt.

number.title: Your certificate number
number.format: Each certificate’s own number: ADA, the credential ({pd} for Postpartum Doula, {bd} for Birth Doula), the year issued and a sequence number.

record.label: Your public record
record.value: Shows your standing today. A certificate shows your status on the day it was issued; the registry record is the primary source.

renewal.intro: Your certification is valid for {validity}. Renew it before the end date on your record to stay in good standing.

need.label: What you need
need.value: One of two pathways, professional reference letters or a recertification exam with a pass mark of {pass}/{max}, and the renewal fee of {fee}.

start.label: How to start
start.value: Check your status and end date in the ADA registry or in My ADA, then contact ADA to begin.

conduct.intro: Every ADA-certified doula is expected to uphold the ADA Code of Conduct.

professional.label: Professional standards
professional.value: Keep your skills and your certification current, practice within your scope, and communicate professionally.

client.label: Client care
client.value: Put the client’s needs at the center of care, seek informed consent, keep client information confidential, respect every family’s culture, and serve all families without discrimination.

ethics.label: Ethics
ethics.value: Represent your credentials honestly, disclose conflicts of interest, keep professional boundaries, report abuse, neglect or safety concerns as the law requires, and cooperate with ADA reviews.

enforcement.label: If the Code is broken
enforcement.value: Violations can lead to suspension or revocation of ADA certification. Anyone can report a concern to <mail>{email}</mail>. Reports are reviewed confidentially.

conduct.readFull: Read the full Code of Conduct

course.q: Where do I take the course?
course.a: With an ADA-approved training program, in person or online. Programs are listed on the <link>ADA education</link> page.

language.q: Can I take the exam in my own language?
language.a: Yes. The exam is offered in {languages}. Choose your language when you register.

check.q: How do families and insurers check my certification?
check.a: They search the ADA registry at <link>{url}</link>. Insurance providers can verify your certification there.
